It also sets `BoxColliderComponent`, `RigidBodyComponent`, `VelocityComponent`, `PlayerState`, `CameraFollowTargetComponent` (lines 30-46), and reads `request.CustomFields` (LDtk-only) to optionally mutate damping (lines 91-97).
**WHY IT BREAKS:** The contract serializes exactly `TransformComponent` + SOURCE `SpriteInfoComponent` + a re-spawn id (items 7/8). On reload it re-dispatches by id (item 9/10). Re-spawning "Player" by id re-runs the factory, which **fabricates a fresh orb sub-tree from scratch** — so it does NOT round-trip the *edited* state of those children: any gizmo move/delete a designer made to an orb is discarded, and conversely the orbs aren't in the saved `entities[]` at all yet reappear on load (count mismatch). Test obligation 1 ("same tagged set") fails the moment a factory spawns children. The plan's flat `entities[]` list has no representation for the parent/child graph that `SetParent`/`ChildOfComponent` builds (CORE_TENETS §3; foundation premise "ChildOfComponent and TransformComponent.Parent are two intentional links").
**attacks:** new-surface (the draft's serialization model assumes 1 spawn-request ⇒ 1 flat entity; the real factories produce parented sub-graphs and game-logic components the model can't capture or even enumerate).

## BLOCKER 2 — There is no asset/texture key on the entity to serialize; the writer's "asset key" field does not exist
**CLAIM ATTACKED:** Contract item 8 ("SOURCE SpriteInfoComponent fields (… layer/asset key)"); §1 finding "the writer stores a factory/asset key, not the live texture"; §4b row "Persisted sort fields".
**EVIDENCE:** `SpriteInfoComponent` (read in full above) has fields `SpriteSheet:Texture2D`, `Source`, `Size`, `Color`, `Target`, `LayerDepth`, `Origin`, `YSortDepthBias`, `YSortOffset`, `Offset` — **and no string asset key**. The texture identity lives only inside the factory: `PlayerEntityFactory.cs:23` `content.Load<Texture2D>("Atlas/TX Player")`; the source rect for LDtk entities is computed from `request.TilesetPosition` (`PlayerEntityFactory.cs:52`), which is itself never stored on the entity.
**WHY IT BREAKS:** The writer cannot "store a factory/asset key" by reading `SpriteInfoComponent` — there is nothing to read. For factory-spawned (LDtk) entities the texture+source are *implied* by the factory id (so the id is the de-facto key — fine), but for **Blender-direct entities** (`BlenderLevelParserSystem.cs:299` `_content.Load<Texture2D>(contentPath)`; `Source` computed by `CalculateSourceRect` from UV at `:319`) there is **no id and no stored key** — GAP-2's recommended "native re-spawn descriptor" would have to invent and persist the content path + the computed source rect + size + origin, none of which is in any component today. The contract presents "asset key" as an existing SOURCE field; it is net-new data the plan does not budget.
**attacks:** new-surface.

## BLOCKER 3 — Same-world overlay cannot toggle into Edit without rebuilding the pipeline: editor systems aren't in the pipeline, and HierarchySystem deletes orphans
**CLAIM ATTACKED:** Contract item 6 ("toggling RunMode enters/exits editing without a screen swap … Update/Draw built once at Load"); precondition diff "Concurrent game + editor in one world … no screen swap"; test obligation 13 ("Same-world overlay … no Dispose/Load").
**EVIDENCE:** `ScreenController.cs:57,62` — `_screen.current.UpdateSystem.Update(_state)` and `.DrawSystem.Update(_state)` are the **only** entry points; the systems are the `SequentialSystem<GameState>` built once in the screen constructor (`LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs:87-88`, `CreateUpdateSystem`/`CreateDrawSystem`). DefaultEcs `SequentialSystem` does not expose or allow mutating its children after construction (the plan concedes this at §1: "`SequentialSystem` doesn't expose children"). So for editor systems to run on RunMode=Edit, they must **already be registered in the pipeline at Load** and sit inert when Play.
**WHY IT BREAKS (two distinct breaks):**
(a) **Inertness is not free.** The reference editor screen would have to compose the *entire* editor system set into the same `SequentialSystem` at Load. The plan acknowledges this (matrix row "Editor systems … RunNormally (Edit-guarded internally)") — but that means the chosen back-compat mechanism (`GatedSystem`, item 2) is *not* what gates the editor systems; they self-guard on `state.RunMode`. So item 6's "without a screen swap" only holds for a **bespoke editor screen** that pre-registered editor systems. An *existing* screen (LoadLevelExampleGameScreen) can never enter Edit without being rebuilt — which is a screen swap. The "no screen swap" claim is true only for a screen purpose-built with editor systems already inside; it cannot retrofit Edit onto a shipped game screen, contradicting C1's framing that the editor runs "the real pipeline" of an existing game.
(b) **HierarchySystem in Edit will delete editor/selection entities.** `HierarchySystem.Update` runs `DisposeOrphans()` **first** (`HierarchySystem.cs:43,55-83`): any entity with `ChildOfComponent` whose parent isn't alive is `Dispose()`d (foundation premise "Children are disposed with their parents"). The plan mandates HierarchySystem stays `RunNormally` in Edit (item 6, matrix, GAP-3). If the editor parents anything (a gizmo handle to its target, a multi-select group, the orb-style child meshes a selected entity already owns) via `ChildOfComponent`, and the parent is deleted by an undo/delete op mid-frame, the cascade dispose runs **in Edit** and silently takes the children too — including potentially the gizmo or selection-marker entities. Test obligation 6 ("edit a parent transform in Edit; assert child WorldPosition updates") will pass, but the delete-coalescing/undo tests (items 10, 13) collide with this uncontrolled cascade.
**attacks:** (a) new-surface; (b) resolution (breaks GAP-3's "HierarchySystem RunNormally in Edit" fix by surfacing the orphan-dispose side effect the fix didn't account for).

---

## HIGH 4 — Native-format load is clobbered by LevelLoadRequestSystem's unconditional `Content.Load` + `Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>` BEFORE any native reader can react
**CLAIM ATTACKED:** Contract item 9 ("distinct format sibling on LoadLevelRequest, not clobbered by the unconditional LDtk Content.Load/Remove"); precondition diff "Native level load dispatch"; §4 finding.
**EVIDENCE:** `LevelLoadRequestSystem.cs:32` subscribes to `LoadLevelRequest` and `:38 On(...)` runs on **every** request with no identifier gate. On a non-LDtk name, `:49` `_content.Load<LDtkLevel>($"World/{levelIdentifier}")` throws (no such xnb), caught at `:69`, and `:75-76` executes `_world.Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>()` + `Remove<CurrentBackgroundColorComponent>()`. The Blender parser coexists only because it **prefix-filters** (`BlenderLevelParserSystem.cs:77` `if (!StartsWith("Blender_")) return;`) and reads its own content stream — it does **not** rely on `CurrentLevelComponent`.
**WHY IT BREAKS:** A 3rd "native sibling" that follows the LDtk *component-driven* pattern (subscribe to `CurrentLevelComponent` added — the engine's documented preferred pattern, CORE_TENETS §6) is dead on arrival: `LevelLoadRequestSystem` will throw on the native name and **remove** `CurrentLevelComponent` in the same dispatch, so the native parser's add-subscription never fires (or fires then gets the singleton yanked). The only safe shape is the **Blender pattern** — a native reader that itself prefix/format-filters `LoadLevelRequest` directly and ignores `CurrentLevelComponent` entirely. The contract's wording ("not clobbered by … Remove") is satisfiable, but **only** by replicating the prefix-hack the plan elsewhere disparages (CORE_TENETS §9 backlog), and the message ordering between two independent `Subscribe`rs to the same message is registration-order-dependent and undocumented — `LevelLoadRequestSystem` is registered first in the reference screen (`LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs:272`), so its `Remove` runs before a later-registered native reader sees the message. The plan does not specify the dispatch discriminator (a `Format` field on `LoadLevelRequest`? a name prefix?) — without it, item 9 is unimplementable as a clean "sibling."
**attacks:** resolution (the draft claims it has solved the clobber; the live double-subscribe + unconditional Remove means the only working solution is the very prefix-hack the plan says it's improving on, and the discriminator is unspecified).

## HIGH 5 — Gizmo meshes on Main will NOT be kept visible by CullingSystem — culling never visits a SpriteInfo-less mesh entity, and game-set Visible on Main flickers
**CLAIM ATTACKED:** Contract item 12 ("renders … via existing mesh generators (on a render target that culling keeps visible)"); §4 matrix row rendering ("cull gives gizmo meshes VisibleComponent").
**EVIDENCE:** `CullingSystem.cs:12` `[With(typeof(SpriteInfoComponent), typeof(TransformComponent))]` — it only iterates entities that have a **`SpriteInfoComponent`**. A gizmo handle is a mesh (`DrawComponent.Type = Mesh`) with no sprite, exactly like the orbs, which carry **no `SpriteInfoComponent`** and set `VisibleComponent` **manually in the factory** (`PlayerEntityFactory.cs:139,187`). `MasterRenderSystem`'s Main pass requires `VisibleComponent` (`MasterRenderSystem.cs:59`) and renders meshes through the **camera view transform** (`:135,220` `dc.WorldMatrix * transformMatrix`).
**WHY IT BREAKS:** (a) The plan's stated mechanism — "culling keeps gizmo meshes visible" — is false: `CullingSystem` never touches a SpriteInfo-less mesh, so it neither adds nor removes `VisibleComponent` on a gizmo. The gizmo must set `VisibleComponent` itself (like the orbs). (b) Mesh on Main is **world-space (camera-transformed)**, not screen-space — so a gizmo drawn on Main scales/translates with camera zoom and pan; "screen-space/overlay gizmo handles" require the **HUD/UI** target (Matrix.Identity, `MasterRenderSystem.cs:135` null-camera branch), not Main. (c) If a gizmo *did* carry a `SpriteInfoComponent` on Main to get auto-culling, the rendering flow doc's named failure mode bites: "Game-set `VisibleComponent` on Main — `CullingSystem` overwrites it next frame; the entity flickers" (`docs/flows/rendering.md:61`). The contract conflates "culling keeps it visible" with the real options (manual Visible like orbs, or HUD target for screen-space), and picks the one that doesn't work.
**attacks:** new-surface (the rendering mechanism the draft names doesn't match the cull/render contract; gizmo target + visibility-ownership is unresolved).

---

## HIGH 6 — Headless editor-op channel collides with replay auto-exit AND with CursorInputSystem reading Mouse directly with no override
**CLAIM ATTACKED:** Contract item 15; test obligation 12 ("no premature auto-exit"); §4b row "Editor-op replay channel"; precondition diff (implicit cursor-injection).
**EVIDENCE:** `CursorInputSystem.cs:15` `Mouse.GetState()` directly, every frame, **unconditionally** — there is no `SkipHardwareRead`/replay branch on the cursor system (unlike `InputMappingSystem`, which has `SkipHardwareRead`, set at `LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs:151`). `InputReplaySystem.cs:94-98`: the instant `_cursor >= _commands.Count && _pressedActions.Count == 0`, it calls `_game.Exit()`.
**WHY IT BREAKS:** (a) To drive selection/gizmo headlessly the plan must inject `CursorInputComponent.ScreenPosition`/`LeftButton…` — but `CursorInputSystem` **overwrites all of those from `Mouse.GetState()` on the very next Update** (`:22-48`, then `NotifyChanged` at `:50`). There is no seam to suppress the hardware read; the plan's "today CursorInputSystem reads Mouse.GetState() directly" finding is correct but the contract offers no concrete suppression hook, and adding one is net work the items don't enumerate. (b) The replay channel auto-exits on drain (`:97`); a headless editor session that issues `select→move→save→undo` (item 15) and then idles will be **killed by `_game.Exit()`** the moment the action queue empties — before assertions can read the saved file. The plan flags this ("accounting for the replay auto-exit-on-drain") but provides no mechanism; item 15 + test 12 require either a non-action editor-op queue that *also* holds the exit open, or a separate run-loop — unspecified.
**attacks:** resolution (the draft says it "accounts for" the auto-exit and the direct-Mouse read, but neither is resolved — the suppression hook and the exit-deferral are named-but-unbuilt).

---

## MEDIUM 7 — Selection "topmost = post-YSort LayerDepth" is unreadable for the entities most likely stacked, because YSort only runs on `[With(VisibleComponent)]` and only on Y-sorted layers
**CLAIM ATTACKED:** Contract item 11; test obligations 7, 8 ("selection reads the key AFTER YSort overwrote LayerDepth"); §4b row "Selection topmost key".
**EVIDENCE:** `YSortSystem.cs:22` `[With(DrawComponent, SpriteInfoComponent, TransformComponent, VisibleComponent)]` AND `:42` early-returns unless `drawLayerMap.TryGetYSortRange(...)` matches — i.e. it only rewrites `LayerDepth` for entities **on a Y-sorted layer** (in the reference, only `GameDrawLayer.Characters`, `LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs:85`). For all non-Y-sorted layers, `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` is whatever `SpritePrepSystem` set from the source — not "post-YSort." Also, a culled entity (no `VisibleComponent`) is never prepped/sorted at all (`docs/flows/rendering.md:44`), so its `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` is stale/uninitialised.
**WHY IT BREAKS:** "Topmost = MAX final post-YSort LayerDepth" (item 11) is only meaningful for currently-visible entities on Y-sorted layers. For two overlapping sprites on a *static* layer, their `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` equals the source `SpriteInfo.LayerDepth` (YSort skipped them), and ties fall through to **insertion index** — which the SelectionSystem cannot observe from `DrawComponent` (the index is internal to `MasterRenderSystem`'s `DrawSet.GetEntities().Select((e,index)…)`, `MasterRenderSystem.cs:140`). So the "last-index tiebreak mirrors MasterRenderSystem.cs:142" claim (item 11) is **not reproducible from outside the render system** — the selection system has no access to that per-pass insertion order. The pick is correct for the camera/Y-sorted case and ambiguous (or wrong) for same-depth static stacks.
**attacks:** new-surface (the tiebreak key the draft mirrors is private to the renderer's per-frame set; selection can't read it).

---

## Claims that HOLD

- **HOLDS: GameState gains a `RunMode` field with default `Play` without touching call sites.** `GameState.cs:5-21` has one ctor `GameState(GameTime)`; `ScreenController.cs:31` constructs `new(new GameTime())`. Adding `public RunMode RunMode { get; set; } = RunMode.Play;` changes no existing call site — back-compat at the field level holds (`GameState.cs`, `ScreenController.cs:31,55-57`).
- **HOLDS: a `GatedSystem<GameState>` decorator can gate without disturbing ungated systems.** All bundled systems implement `ISystem<GameState>` with their own `IsEnabled` (e.g. `LevelLoadRequestSystem.cs:35`, `CameraFollowSystem.cs:16`); an unwrapped system is byte-identical. Opt-in gating is mechanically sound — the back-compat *field* claim (item 2/precondition row 1) holds; the *screen-level* "byte-identical" claim is only as good as not wrapping anything in shipped screens, which the reference screen (`LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs`) doesn't.
- **HOLDS: CameraFollowSystem has its own `IsEnabled` so a Freeze gate composes with it.** `CameraFollowSystem.cs:16`; gating it off in Edit and writing `Camera.Position` directly is consistent (the system only writes `_camera.Position` at `:91`).
- **HOLDS: serializing SOURCE sort fields (not derived `DrawComponent.LayerDepth`) is the correct call.** `YSortSystem.cs:54` overwrites `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` per-frame from `WorldPosition.Y` + source `SpriteInfo` fields within camera bounds; persisting it would bake one camera frame. The SOURCE fields (`SpriteInfo.LayerDepth/YSortOffset/YSortDepthBias`) exist and are stable (`SpriteInfoComponent` confirmed). Item 8's "NOT the per-frame-derived LayerDepth" is correct.

---

### Net
The run-state field is back-compat-safe (the one thing the plan most loudly claims). The plan's **serialization completeness is broken** (BLOCKER 1 parent/child sub-graphs + game-logic components; BLOCKER 2 no asset key field), the **same-world toggle can't retrofit existing screens and HierarchySystem's orphan-dispose runs in Edit** (BLOCKER 3), the **native-load dispatch only works by re-using the prefix-hack and is unspecified** (HIGH 4), the **gizmo rendering mechanism is mis-stated** (HIGH 5), the **headless channel is named-but-unbuilt against two real blockers** (HIGH 6), and the **selection tiebreak key is private to the renderer** (MEDIUM 7). The biggest gap is exactly where the prompt predicted: round-trip fidelity for factory sub-graphs and Blender-direct entities.

## 9. Deep-plan refutation findings + resolutions (independent refuter, code-grounded)

The first-cut contract assumed `1 spawn-request ⇒ 1 flat entity`; the live factories disprove it. Resolutions below are folded into the Contract once GAP-A is decided.

- **BLOCKER 1 — factories build sub-graphs, not flat entities.** `PlayerEntityFactory.cs:25-145` spawns a parent + blue-orb child (`SetParent:111`) + 3 red grandchildren (`:142-159`) and sets `BoxCollider`/`RigidBody`/`Velocity`/`PlayerState`/`CameraFollowTarget`. Serializing `Transform+SpriteInfo+id` and re-running the factory loses edited children and mismatches the saved count; a flat `entities[]` can't hold the `ChildOfComponent` graph. → **GAP-A** (serialization model).
- **BLOCKER 2 — no asset key on the entity.** `SpriteInfoComponent` holds a live `Texture2D`, no string key; factory entities imply texture via the factory id, but Blender-direct entities (`BlenderLevelParserSystem.cs:299` content path, `:319` computed source rect) have neither id nor stored key. → **GAP-A** (descriptor must carry a sprite-prop key for direct entities) + **GAP-B** (Blender round-trip cost).
- **BLOCKER 3 — same-world overlay constraints.** (a) Editor systems must be pre-registered in the one `SequentialSystem` at Load (can't retrofit a shipped screen) → the editor is a **purpose-built editor screen** running the real game systems + editor systems (inert in Play); "no screen swap" holds *within* it (revises item 6). (b) `HierarchySystem.DisposeOrphans` (`:43,55-83`) runs first and disposes children of dead parents *in Edit* → **editor-overlay entities (gizmo/selection/toolbar) are standalone, never `ChildOfComponent`-parented to game entities; delete is an undo-command that snapshots the disposed sub-graph** (so undo can restore it).
- **HIGH 4 — native load needs its own message.** `LevelLoadRequestSystem.cs:38` runs on every `LoadLevelRequest`, `:49` throws on a non-LDtk name, `:75` `Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>`. → **The native scene reader subscribes to a dedicated `LoadSceneRequest` message + native parser, NOT `LoadLevelRequest`** (revises item 9; avoids the clobber and the prefix-hack, and doesn't touch `LevelLoadRequestSystem`).
- **HIGH 5 — gizmo visibility/space.** `CullingSystem.cs:12` only iterates `[With(SpriteInfoComponent)]`; mesh gizmos have no sprite, so culling never sets `VisibleComponent` on them. → **Gizmo/selection-highlight entities set `VisibleComponent` themselves** (like the orbs at `PlayerEntityFactory.cs:139,187`), drawn world-space on Main (optionally scaled by `1/Zoom` for constant screen size) (revises item 12 — drops the false "culling keeps them visible").
- **HIGH 6 — headless channel work is real.** `CursorInputSystem.cs:15` reads `Mouse.GetState()` unconditionally (no `SkipHardwareRead` seam, unlike `InputMappingSystem`); `InputReplaySystem.cs:97` auto-exits on drain. → **Add a `SkipHardwareRead` flag to `CursorInputSystem` (mirror the input-mapping precedent) so injected cursor state survives, and an editor-op channel that holds the session open** (revises item 15 — budgets both as explicit work).
- **MEDIUM 7 — selection tiebreak.** `YSortSystem` only rewrites `LayerDepth` for `[With(VisibleComponent)]` on Y-sorted layers; the insertion-index tiebreak is private to `MasterRenderSystem.cs:140`'s per-frame set. → **Selection picks MAX final `LayerDepth`; exact-depth ties resolved by a selection-owned deterministic tiebreak (not the renderer's private index)** (revises item 11).
- **HOLDS:** `GameState.RunMode` default `Play` is back-compat at the field + call sites (`GameState.cs:5`, `ScreenController.cs:31,55-57`); opt-in `GatedSystem` doesn't disturb ungated systems; camera-follow's own `IsEnabled` composes with a Freeze gate; serializing SOURCE sort fields (not derived `DrawComponent.LayerDepth`) is correct.

### GAPs requiring a human decision (surfaced at approval)

## 9. Deep-plan refutation findings + resolutions (independent refuter, code-grounded)

The first-cut contract assumed `1 spawn-request ⇒ 1 flat entity`; the live factories disprove it. Resolutions below are folded into the Contract once GAP-A is decided.

- **BLOCKER 1 — factories build sub-graphs, not flat entities.** `PlayerEntityFactory.cs:25-145` spawns a parent + blue-orb child (`SetParent:111`) + 3 red grandchildren (`:142-159`) and sets `BoxCollider`/`RigidBody`/`Velocity`/`PlayerState`/`CameraFollowTarget`. Serializing `Transform+SpriteInfo+id` and re-running the factory loses edited children and mismatches the saved count; a flat `entities[]` can't hold the `ChildOfComponent` graph. → **GAP-A** (serialization model).
- **BLOCKER 2 — no asset key on the entity.** `SpriteInfoComponent` holds a live `Texture2D`, no string key; factory entities imply texture via the factory id, but Blender-direct entities (`BlenderLevelParserSystem.cs:299` content path, `:319` computed source rect) have neither id nor stored key. → **GAP-A** (descriptor must carry a sprite-prop key for direct entities) + **GAP-B** (Blender round-trip cost).
- **BLOCKER 3 — same-world overlay constraints.** (a) Editor systems must be pre-registered in the one `SequentialSystem` at Load (can't retrofit a shipped screen) → the editor is a **purpose-built editor screen** running the real game systems + editor systems (inert in Play); "no screen swap" holds *within* it (revises item 6). (b) `HierarchySystem.DisposeOrphans` (`:43,55-83`) runs first and disposes children of dead parents *in Edit* → **editor-overlay entities (gizmo/selection/toolbar) are standalone, never `ChildOfComponent`-parented to game entities; delete is an undo-command that snapshots the disposed sub-graph** (so undo can restore it).
- **HIGH 4 — native load needs its own message.** `LevelLoadRequestSystem.cs:38` runs on every `LoadLevelRequest`, `:49` throws on a non-LDtk name, `:75` `Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>`. → **The native scene reader subscribes to a dedicated `LoadSceneRequest` message + native parser, NOT `LoadLevelRequest`** (revises item 9; avoids the clobber and the prefix-hack, and doesn't touch `LevelLoadRequestSystem`).
- **HIGH 5 — gizmo visibility/space.** `CullingSystem.cs:12` only iterates `[With(SpriteInfoComponent)]`; mesh gizmos have no sprite, so culling never sets `VisibleComponent` on them. → **Gizmo/selection-highlight entities set `VisibleComponent` themselves** (like the orbs at `PlayerEntityFactory.cs:139,187`), drawn world-space on Main (optionally scaled by `1/Zoom` for constant screen size) (revises item 12 — drops the false "culling keeps them visible").
- **HIGH 6 — headless channel work is real.** `CursorInputSystem.cs:15` reads `Mouse.GetState()` unconditionally (no `SkipHardwareRead` seam, unlike `InputMappingSystem`); `InputReplaySystem.cs:97` auto-exits on drain. → **Add a `SkipHardwareRead` flag to `CursorInputSystem` (mirror the input-mapping precedent) so injected cursor state survives, and an editor-op channel that holds the session open** (revises item 15 — budgets both as explicit work).

content.text: These findings sharpen the one fork the spec itself called the **highest-impact decision** (2.3): the *unit of save*. My first cut (flat `Transform+SpriteInfo+id`) is provably wrong against the real factories. Here's the fork, plus the Blender-scope question and final approval.

questions.question: Serialization model (GAP-A) — what is the unit of save, given factories build parent+child sub-graphs and set physics/state components? This decides what's editable/savable in Wave A.

options.label: Re-spawn descriptor + overrides (Recommended)
options.description: Each tagged ROOT stores how to recreate it (factory{id,params} OR sprite{asset,src,size,origin}) + editor transform/sprite overrides. On load: re-run factory / make prop, apply overrides. Factory-internal children (e.g. Player's orbs) stay factory-owned — regenerated, not independently edited in Wave A. Reuses factories (cornerstone-aligned), bounded; cost: can't independently edit factory-spawned children yet.

options.label: Full component serialization
options.description: A per-component-type serializer registry writes/reads EVERY serializable component + the parent/child graph. Anything round-trips exactly and is editable. Cost: a large net-new serialization layer, and it drifts from 'factories are the one creation authority'.

options.label: Prop-only for Wave A
options.description: Only simple Transform+Sprite 'prop' entities (no children, no physics) are taggable/editable/savable now; complex factory/gameplay entities are view-only. Smallest scope; cost: a designer can't reposition or save a gameplay entity in Wave A.

questions.question: Blender-origin entity save (GAP-B) — Blender-direct entities have no factory id and no stored asset key (only a content path + computed source rect at parse time). Round-trip them now, or defer?

options.label: Capture descriptor at parse-time (Recommended)
options.description: The Blender parser tags entities + records a sprite re-spawn descriptor (content path + computed source rect + size/origin) so Blender-authored props round-trip through save/load. Net-new descriptor data captured at parse; lets a designer edit+save a Blender level's props.

options.label: Defer Blender-origin save
options.description: Wave A round-trips only editor-placed + factory-spawned entities; editing/saving Blender-origin props waits for a later wave. Smaller Wave A; cost: Blender-authored props are view-only in the editor for now.

questions.question: Final approval of the hardened plan (with the recommended resolutions for the other refuter findings: purpose-built editor screen, dedicated LoadSceneRequest, manual gizmo VisibleComponent, CursorInputSystem SkipHardwareRead seam)?

options.label: Approve
options.description: Finalize the plan with the choices above, stamp APPROVED, and hand off to /implement (preflight on feat/level-editor → wave-by-wave implementation + ledger → verify → open PR → auto-chain review-fix-loop). Each autonomous decision will be documented in the PR.

options.label: Cancel

Only tagged entities participate in save; transient cursor/UI/HUD/gizmo/overlay entities are excluded.
8. A scene **writer** queries `[With(SceneObjectComponent)]` and serializes, per entity: `TransformComponent` (pos/rot/scale/origin) + the **SOURCE** `SpriteInfoComponent` fields (`LayerDepth`, `YSortOffset`, `YSortDepthBias`, layer/asset key) + the re-spawn identifier — **NOT** the per-frame-derived `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` and **NOT** the live `Texture2D`. Plus `camera` + `layers[]`. Written through `IPlatformServices` (desktop file; web download/clipboard member).
9. A scene **reader** is dispatched as a **distinct format sibling on `LoadLevelRequest`** (not clobbered by the unconditional LDtk `Content.Load`/`Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>`); reconstructs entities via a transform-carrying spawn path (see item 9b); **fails loud on an unknown re-spawn identifier** (today's dispatch silently drops). Round-trip: save→reload reproduces the same tagged-entity set + transforms + layer assignment, and a frame of draw-prep+YSort recomputes `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` identically to pre-save.
10. **Native spawn path (resolves GAP-1):** the reader does not reuse the LDtk-shaped `EntitySpawnRequest` verbatim; it uses a transform-carrying spawn path (chosen option recorded in the plan — see §7 GAP-1) so native scene data needn't fabricate LDtk `LayerInstance`/`Pivot`/`TilesetPosition`.
input.new_string:
6. A **purpose-built reference editor screen** (Examples.Core) composes editor systems over the game pipeline in the **same world**, with editor systems **pre-registered** (inert in `Play`, since `SequentialSystem` can't be mutated post-Load); toggling `RunMode` enters/exits editing **without a screen swap** (no `Dispose`/`Load`, world state preserved). Per the Matrix (§4): physics/velocity/collision/orb/NPC/dialogue/camera-follow `Freeze`; **`HierarchySystem` + the world-cache/transform-propagation path stay `RunNormally`/`RunPartial`** so editor edits propagate; cull/prep/sort/render and input/cursor `RunNormally`. **Editor-overlay entities (gizmo/selection/toolbar) are standalone — never `ChildOfComponent`-parented to game entities** — so `HierarchySystem.DisposeOrphans` (which runs in Edit) cannot cascade-dispose them; **delete is an undo-command that snapshots the disposed sub-graph** so it can be restored.
7. **Membership (GAP-A = full serialization):** `SceneObjectComponent` tags save-root entities; the writer includes each tagged root **plus its `ChildOfComponent` descendants**, so factory sub-graphs (e.g. a Player + its orbiting children) round-trip exactly with the parent graph intact. Transient cursor/UI/HUD/gizmo/editor-overlay entities are untagged → excluded. Blender-origin entities are untagged in Wave A (GAP-B deferred) → view-only.
8. A **component-serializer registry**: the engine ships `(write,read)` serializers for its serializable components (`TransformComponent`, `SpriteInfoComponent`, colliders, `RigidBody`/`Velocity`, mesh `DrawComponent` params, layer/ySort SOURCE fields, the `ChildOf`/parent link); **game code registers serializers for its own components** (e.g. `PlayerState`) — the registry is the extension seam (framework-not-library). The scene **writer** serializes every *registered* component of every in-scope entity to `entities[]` (each with `components{}` + a `parent` ref) + `camera` + `layers[]`. `Texture2D` is serialized as an **asset key** (an additive optional `AssetKey` on `SpriteInfoComponent`, set at creation by factories/editor-placement), **never the live texture**; SOURCE sort fields (`SpriteInfo.LayerDepth`/`YSortOffset`/`YSortDepthBias`), **never the per-frame-derived `DrawComponent.LayerDepth`**. An **unregistered component type is skipped with a loud warning** (visible gap, never silent). Written through `IPlatformServices` (desktop file; new web download/clipboard member).
9. A scene **reader** subscribes to a **dedicated `LoadSceneRequest` message** (NOT `LoadLevelRequest` — avoids `LevelLoadRequestSystem`'s unconditional LDtk `Content.Load`/`Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>` clobber). It reconstructs in **two passes** — create all entities + deserialize each `components{}` via the registry (rehydrating `Texture2D` from the asset key), then wire the `parent` graph — and **fails loud on an unregistered component type** found in the file. Round-trip: save→`LoadSceneRequest` reproduces the same entity set (incl. sub-graph children) + all serialized components + parent graph; one draw-prep+YSort frame recomputes `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` identically to pre-save. (Factories remain the *authoring* path for new entities; the registry is the *round-trip* path — native load never goes through the LDtk-shaped `EntitySpawnRequest`.)
10. The registry is **opt-in per component type** (only registered types serialize), so engine tags and transient state (`VisibleComponent`, cursor state, editor-overlay markers) are never written; registration happens at module/screen init so the in-scope component set is explicit and greppable.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# deep-plan PR gate — PreToolUse hook on Bash. (Optional; wire it up in the consuming
# repo's .claude/settings.json as a PreToolUse(Bash) hook to enable.)
#
# Blocks `gh pr create` on a branch that touches a SENSITIVE domain unless a COMPLETE
# plan-contract exists (a `## Contract` block, no GATE FAIL, no unjustified GAP,
# Residual GAPs: 0). Which domains are sensitive is read from the repo's config
# (docs/agents/skills-config.md › Sensitive domains) — NOT hardcoded. If the repo
# declares no sensitive domains (or has no config), the gate never blocks.
#
# Fail-open by design: any ambiguity that isn't a clear "incomplete contract on a
# sensitive branch" allows the command through. The override token is always available.
#
# Contract:
#   exit 0            -> allow the gh pr create
#   exit 2 + stderr   -> block; stderr is surfaced to the agent (PreToolUse convention)
#
# Override: put `[deep-plan-override: <reason>]` anywhere in the gh pr create args, or
# set env DEEP_PLAN_OVERRIDE=<reason>. Audited to stderr but always allows.

set -uo pipefail

PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}"
if [ -z "$PROJECT_DIR" ]; then
  PROJECT_DIR="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
fi
CONFIG="$PROJECT_DIR/docs/agents/skills-config.md"

# --- 1. Read the tool input and extract the bash command -------------------
if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
  payload="$(cat 2>/dev/null || true)"
else
  payload=""
fi
cmd="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | python3 -c 'import sys,json
try:
    d=json.load(sys.stdin)
    print((d.get("tool_input") or {}).get("command",""))
except Exception:
    print("")' 2>/dev/null || true)"

# --- 2. Only act on `gh pr create` -----------------------------------------
case "$cmd" in
  *"gh pr create"*) : ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

# --- 3. Override ------------------------------------------------------------
if [ -n "${DEEP_PLAN_OVERRIDE:-}" ]; then
  echo "deep-plan PR gate: overridden via DEEP_PLAN_OVERRIDE=${DEEP_PLAN_OVERRIDE} — allowing." >&2
  exit 0
fi
case "$cmd" in
  *"[deep-plan-override:"*)
    echo "deep-plan PR gate: overridden via [deep-plan-override:] token in PR args — allowing." >&2
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

cd "$PROJECT_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0

# --- 4. Which domains are sensitive? (from config, not hardcoded) ----------
# Extract the comma-separated token list under "## Sensitive domains" — the first line
# in that section that is purely lowercase identifiers separated by commas (prose
# explainer lines and `<!-- -->` comments are skipped; `none`/`(none …)` yields nothing).
sensitive_regex() {
  [ -f "$CONFIG" ] || return 1
  awk '
    /^##[[:space:]]+[Ss]ensitive domains/ {inblk=1; next}
    inblk && /^##[[:space:]]/ {inblk=0}
    inblk {print}
  ' "$CONFIG" \
  | sed 's/<!--.*-->//' | tr -d '`' \
  | while IFS= read -r line; do
      t="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
      [ -z "$t" ] && continue
      if printf '%s' "$t" | grep -qE '^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*([[:space:]]*,[[:space:]]*[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)*$'; then
        printf '%s' "$t" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g' \
          | grep -vxE '(none|empty)' | grep -E '^[a-z]'
        break
      fi
    done | sort -u | paste -sd'|' -
}

SENS_RE="$(sensitive_regex || true)"
# No config, or no sensitive domains declared → gate does not apply.
[ -z "$SENS_RE" ] && exit 0

changed="$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
[ -z "$changed" ] && changed="$(git diff --name-only origin/main 2>/dev/null || true)"
if ! printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -Eq "($SENS_RE)"; then
  exit 0  # not a sensitive-domain change — gate does not apply.
fi

# --- 5. Find a complete plan-contract for this repo ------------------------
is_complete_contract() {
  local f="$1"
  grep -Eq '^##+ *Contract' "$f" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  grep -Eiq 'gate[*_: ]+fail' "$f" 2>/dev/null && return 1
  if grep -Eiq 'residual gaps' "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    grep -Eiq 'residual gaps[^0-9]*0' "$f" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  fi
  if grep -Eiq '\| *GAP *\|' "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

found_complete=0
checked=0

# 5a. Repo-local contract artifacts committed ON THIS BRANCH (most robust).
if [ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/deep-plan" ]; then
  for f in "$PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/deep-plan/*.md; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    rel="${f#"$PROJECT_DIR"/}"
    printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -Fq "$rel" || continue
    checked=$((checked+1))
    if is_complete_contract "$f"; then found_complete=1; break; fi
  done
fi

# 5b. Session plans describing THIS branch's change. Repo-local .claude/.plans/ first
# (where /refine writes; gitignored), then the global ~/.claude/plans/. "Belongs" means
# the plan references a file this branch actually changes.
scan_plans_dir() {
  local plans_dir="$1"
  [ -d "$plans_dir" ] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    grep -Eq '^##+ *Contract' "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
    belongs=0
    while IFS= read -r tok; do
      [ -n "$tok" ] || continue
      if printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -Fq "$tok"; then belongs=1; break; fi
    done < <(grep -oE '[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+' "$f" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | head -40)
    [ "$belongs" -eq 1 ] || continue
    checked=$((checked+1))
    if is_complete_contract "$f"; then found_complete=1; return 0; fi
  done < <(ls -t "$plans_dir"/*.md 2>/dev/null | head -10)
}

[ "$found_complete" -eq 0 ] && scan_plans_dir "$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/.plans"
[ "$found_complete" -eq 0 ] && scan_plans_dir "$HOME/.claude/plans"

if [ "$found_complete" -eq 1 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# --- 6. Block --------------------------------------------------------------
cat >&2 <<EOF
🚫 deep-plan PR gate: blocked.

This branch touches a sensitive domain ($(printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -Eo "($SENS_RE)" | sort -u | paste -sd, -)) but no COMPLETE plan-contract was found (checked $checked candidate(s)).

Before opening this PR:
  1. Author/finish the plan-contract — run /deep-plan (it fills the interaction matrix,
     dimension table, and precondition diff, and gates on completeness).
  2. Run /verify-plan and resolve every Missing / Diverged / unresolved-GAP.
  3. Make the contract discoverable: deep-plan's "write artifacts" option, or commit it
     under .claude/deep-plan/<branch>.md.

A complete contract has a "## Contract" block and no incompleteness markers: no
"Gate: FAIL", "Residual GAPs: 0" (when present), no bare "| GAP |" cells.

Sensitive domains are read from docs/agents/skills-config.md › Sensitive domains. To
override for a genuine exception (audited): add [deep-plan-override: <reason>] to the
gh pr create args, or set DEEP_PLAN_OVERRIDE=<reason>.
EOF
exit 2

1. **Cornerstone C1 — the editor IS the game.** It is an in-game *mode* running the REAL pipeline (`CullingSystem → SpritePrepSystem → YSortSystem → MasterRenderSystem`) and the REAL `Camera`. Do NOT build a separate editor renderer or a parallel editor data model. The editor previews exactly what the player sees.
2. **Cornerstone C2 — editor tooling = ECS systems + components on top of the game's systems**, gated by a NEW engine-wide system run-state model (`GameState.RunMode` Play/Edit + per-system edit-time policy + `GatedSystem` decorator). **The engine DOCS MUST codify this** (a `CORE_TENETS` tenet + a `foundation` premise) — this is non-negotiable, because the gamedev's AI agents deliver Waves B–F and need the contract written down.
3. **Lay the foundation for the WHOLE process**, not just Wave A code. Ship `docs/level-editor/roadmap.md` mapping Waves A–F (seams, dependencies, decisions made vs deferred, plug-in points) + the new `level-editor` module skeleton + the run-state model + the native scene format spec, so a fresh Claude Code session can implement B–F without re-deriving the architecture.
4. **Performance (edit-time AND runtime).** Unifying rule: bake sources at load, NEVER re-evaluate parametric sources per frame. Y-sort is per-frame per-visible-entity and re-sorts on camera move (dense scatter = a FUTURE Wave-D hotspot). Keep editor systems cheap.
5. **ECS purity (CORE_TENETS).** Components are pure data; behavior in systems. Undo entries are DATA + an applying system, not OO command objects with embedded behavior where avoidable.
6. **Decisions locked at approval:**
   - GAP-A = **full component serialization** via an extensible registry (engine ships serializers for its components; game registers its own — e.g. `PlayerState`); preserve the parent/child graph; round-trip reconstructs from components, NOT by re-running factories. `Texture2D` → an additive optional `AssetKey` on `SpriteInfoComponent`.
   - GAP-B = **defer Blender-origin save** (Blender props view-only in Wave A; untagged).

The `.claude/workflows/deep-plan.js` and `implement.js` (and likely `review-fix-loop.js`) workflows force their agents to return results via a **StructuredOutput schema with tight per-field char caps** (deep-plan matrix: ~240 chars/cell; implement Setup: goal ≤400, contractItem ≤200, planSummary ≤600). On a large, detail-heavy task they fail identically: `StructuredOutput retry cap (5) exceeded — no valid output` → the workflow hard-throws. **Why:** the model can't compress that much real detail under the caps within 5 retries; it's deterministic at scale, so **resuming re-crashes at the same serialization step**.

**How to apply:** For a large task, don't rely on these workflows end-to-end. (a) Harvest the partial work — the analyze slices / wave split are usually persisted (journal.jsonl `result` records; the ledger) even when the workflow throws. (b) Recover by driving the work with **plain `Agent` subagents (general-purpose / Explore) that return plain text** — they have no forced StructuredOutput schema and never hit this. (c) Or patch the caps in the workflow script and resume (invasive — edits repo-tracked tooling). The plain-agent fallback is what actually delivered. # MonoDreams Project Memory

## Project Structure (Post-Refactor)
- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library with rendering, camera, cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading
- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific: screens, input, dialogue, layout, settings, entity factories
- `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/` — isolated YarnSpinner integration (not referenced by core)
- Build: `dotnet build` for everything; individual projects can be built separately

## Key Architecture Decisions
- **EntityInfo** is string-based in core (`new EntityInfo("Player")`), Examples has `EntityType` enum convenience
- **Namespace conflicts**: `MonoDreams.EntityFactory` (not `.Entity`) to avoid shadowing `DefaultEcs.Entity`
- **CameraFollowTarget** lives in `MonoDreams.Component` (not Camera subdir) to avoid conflict with `Camera` class
- Core has no implicit usings — always add `using System;`, `using System.Collections.Generic;`, `using System.Linq;` when moving files from Examples to core

## Refactoring Patterns
- When moving files: use `cp` + `sed` (not cat/heredoc) so user can cache permissions in Claude Code
- Always `sed -i ''` on macOS (BSD sed requires empty string for in-place editing)
- After moving files from Examples to core, check for empty directories and remove them
- Build after every phase to catch issues early

**One decision worth your eyes (affects Wave 3 test design):**

So a full Player sub-graph round-trips its *graph and data* but the orbs lose their *visual*. For Wave A — whose real edit targets are sprite "props" — this is reasonable, and it means the Wave 3 round-trip golden test should center on **sprite entities**.

input.content:
## Summary

Introduces the **in-game level editor** for MonoDreams — the *foundation* + *Wave A* (the authoring substrate). Two cornerstones drive the design:

- **The editor is the game.** Editing is an in-game **mode** that runs the real render pipeline (`CullingSystem → SpritePrepSystem → YSortSystem → MasterRenderSystem`) and the real `Camera`, so the designer composes against exactly what the player sees (no separate editor renderer, no parallel data model).
- **Editor tooling = ECS systems + components on top of the game's systems**, gated by a new engine-wide **system run-state model**. The engine docs codify this contract (a `CORE_TENETS` tenet + a `foundation` premise) so future work — and future AI agents — can build Waves B–F on it.

Scope is **Wave A only**; Waves B–F (stroke sampler, free placement, scatter, ground, road) are mapped in `docs/level-editor/roadmap.md` for a future session, not implemented here.

## What's in this PR (by seam)

- **Foundation — system run-state model:** `GameState.RunMode` (`Play`/`Edit`, default `Play`), an `EditTimeBehavior` policy enum, and a `GatedSystem` decorator. Opt-in only — a screen that never wraps a system or never sets `Edit` is byte-identical to before.
- **Persistence:** a game-extensible **component-serializer registry** (opt-in per type; unregistered components are warn-skipped on write, fail-loud on read), an additive optional `AssetKey` on `SpriteInfoComponent` (so a non-serializable `Texture2D` round-trips as a content key), the native **MonoDreams scene format** (`version`/`camera`/`layers[]`/reserved `sources[]`/`entities[]` with `components{}` + `parent`), a scene **writer** via `IPlatformServices`, and a **reader on a dedicated `LoadSceneRequest`** message (deliberately *not* `LoadLevelRequest`, so the LDtk loader's unconditional `Content.Load`/`Remove` never clobbers it).
- **Interactive editor (`LevelEditorScreen`, Examples.Core):** a same-world overlay — game logic + camera-follow wrapped in `GatedSystem(Freeze)`, `HierarchySystem` kept live so edits propagate; `F1` toggles `Play`↔`Edit` with no screen swap. Selection (topmost by final post-YSort `LayerDepth` + a selection-owned tiebreak), a transform gizmo (move/rotate/scale, grid-snap, one drag = one undo step), bounded undo/redo (FIFO eviction; delete snapshots the sub-graph), and an engine-native toolbar on the HUD (no ImGui).
- **Headless:** a `CursorInputSystem.SkipHardwareRead` seam + an editor-op channel (`EditorOpPlan`/`EditorOpReplaySystem`) that drives select→drag→undo→save with no real mouse, holding the session open past replay drain.
- **Docs:** new `level-editor` module (count 13→14), CORE_TENETS §9 *"The editor is part of the game"*, foundation + level-editor premises (all `Tests:` filled), the scene-format spec, and the A–F roadmap.

## Test plan

- **Full Release gate (green):** `dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj -c Release` → 0 errors; `dotnet test --configuration Release` → **MonoDreams.Tests 94/0/0**, **MonoDreams.Cli.Tests 31/0**.
- **Web head (green):** `dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples.Web -p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web` → 0 errors (the `IPlatformServices`/platform seam compiles on KNI/BlazorGL).
- **§6 coverage** — every obligation has a named test: round-trip golden, derived-depth reproduction, membership filter, run-state gating (+in-editor-screen), back-compat default, hierarchy-live-in-Edit, selection topmost + ordering, undo bounded-cap, drag-coalescing, gizmo+snap, same-world overlay + delete-snapshot, and the headless editor-op integration test (select→drag→undo→save, no mouse).
- **Manual:** `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples.Desktop`, open `LevelEditorScreen`, press `F1` to enter edit mode.

## verify-plan reconciliation (vs the committed contract)

All **16 contract items delivered** (coverage complete; no Missing). The divergences are the deliberate, pre-approved scope reductions listed under *Known follow-ups*. No unplanned logic of note. No new premise ships `Tests: none yet` (the pre-existing `none yet` entries in foundation/camera/collision/etc. predate this branch). Contract: `.claude/deep-plan/feat-level-editor-6fbd191.md`.

## Decisions taken autonomously

(Surfaced and approved interactively during planning; recorded here for review.)

- **GAP-A = full component serialization** (chosen over a re-spawn-descriptor): reconstruct entities from serialized components + the `ChildOf` parent graph, not by re-running factories — so factory sub-graphs and edited child state round-trip exactly.
- **`LoadSceneRequest` is a dedicated message**, not `LoadLevelRequest` — avoids `LevelLoadRequestSystem`'s unconditional LDtk `Content.Load`/`Remove<CurrentLevelComponent>` clobber.
- **Selection tiebreak = a selection-owned `EditorIdComponent`** (creation order), not the renderer's private per-frame insertion index (which isn't observable outside `MasterRenderSystem`).
- **`SelectionSystem` runs at the end of the Draw pipeline** so it reads the post-YSort `LayerDepth` of the current frame.
- **Gizmo:** analytic world-space hit-test sized by `1/Zoom`; drag uses the immutable drag-start pivot so snap doesn't drift; one `CompositeCommand` per drag.
- **Toolbar on the HUD target** (not `AutoLayoutBuilder`'s Main default), hidden in Play by blanking; `GatedSystem` is non-generic (only `GameState` carries `RunMode`).
- **Editor-op channel is a separate frame-indexed driver** (not an extension of the keyboard-only `InputReplayPlan`); hold-open via a new `InputReplaySystem.SuppressAutoExit` predicate.

## Known follow-ups (deferred; none blocking Wave A)

1. **Web `ExportScene` is a stub** — desktop file-save works fully; the real Blazor browser-download/clipboard path is a TODO.
2. **LDtk-tileset sprites round-trip with a null `AssetKey`** (editor-placed + Player/NPC-factory entities set it; LDtk-origin sprites would need a tileset key at the parser).
3. **Mesh `DrawComponent` serialization deferred to Wave F** — the round-trip is sprite-focused; mesh-only entities keep data/graph but not their visual.
4. **Blender-origin save deferred (GAP-B)** — Blender-authored props are view-only in the editor for now.
5. **The headless editor-op test is in-process** over the real systems (not a process-host run), because `SelectionSystem` lives in the Draw pipeline and the Examples headless host early-returns `Draw`; a render-capable headless mode is backlog (CORE_TENETS §10).

## Summary

Introduces the **in-game level editor** for MonoDreams — the *foundation* + *Wave A* (the authoring substrate). Two cornerstones drive the design:

- **The editor is the game.** Editing is an in-game **mode** that runs the real render pipeline (`CullingSystem → SpritePrepSystem → YSortSystem → MasterRenderSystem`) and the real `Camera`, so the designer composes against exactly what the player sees (no separate editor renderer, no parallel data model).
- **Editor tooling = ECS systems + components on top of the game's systems**, gated by a new engine-wide **system run-state model**. The engine docs codify this contract (a `CORE_TENETS` tenet + a `foundation` premise) so future work — and future AI agents — can build Waves B–F on it.

Scope is **Wave A only**; Waves B–F (stroke sampler, free placement, scatter, ground, road) are mapped in `docs/level-editor/roadmap.md` for a future session, not implemented here.

## What's in this PR (by seam)

- **Foundation — system run-state model:** `GameState.RunMode` (`Play`/`Edit`, default `Play`), an `EditTimeBehavior` policy enum, and a `GatedSystem` decorator. Opt-in only — a screen that never wraps a system or never sets `Edit` is byte-identical to before.
- **Persistence:** a game-extensible **component-serializer registry** (opt-in per type; unregistered components are warn-skipped on write, fail-loud on read), an additive optional `AssetKey` on `SpriteInfoComponent` (so a non-serializable `Texture2D` round-trips as a content key), the native **MonoDreams scene format** (`version`/`camera`/`layers[]`/reserved `sources[]`/`entities[]` with `components{}` + `parent`), a scene **writer** via `IPlatformServices`, and a **reader on a dedicated `LoadSceneRequest`** message (deliberately *not* `LoadLevelRequest`, so the LDtk loader's unconditional `Content.Load`/`Remove` never clobbers it).
- **Interactive editor (`LevelEditorScreen`, Examples.Core):** a same-world overlay — game logic + camera-follow wrapped in `GatedSystem(Freeze)`, `HierarchySystem` kept live so edits propagate; `F1` toggles `Play`↔`Edit` with no screen swap. Selection (topmost by final post-YSort `LayerDepth` + a selection-owned tiebreak), a transform gizmo (move/rotate/scale, grid-snap, one drag = one undo step), bounded undo/redo (FIFO eviction; delete snapshots the sub-graph), and an engine-native toolbar on the HUD (no ImGui).
- **Headless:** a `CursorInputSystem.SkipHardwareRead` seam + an editor-op channel (`EditorOpPlan`/`EditorOpReplaySystem`) that drives select→drag→undo→save with no real mouse, holding the session open past replay drain.
- **Docs:** new `level-editor` module (count 13→14), CORE_TENETS §9 *"The editor is part of the game"*, foundation + level-editor premises (all `Tests:` filled), the scene-format spec, and the A–F roadmap.

- **GAP-A = full component serialization** (chosen over a re-spawn-descriptor): reconstruct entities from serialized components + the `ChildOf` parent graph, not by re-running factories — so factory sub-graphs and edited child state round-trip exactly.

## How to test it (no `Game1` edits needed now)

```
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples.Desktop
```

1. In the level-selection menu, click the **Edit** button next to a level (Level 1 = `Level_0` LDtk, Level 2 = `Blender_Level`).
2. The editor boots on that level. Press **F1** → enter **Edit** mode (toolbar appears on the HUD; game logic freezes).
3. Press **Home** → frame the camera on the level's content. *(Do this for `Blender_Level` especially — its content is at ~(1275,−530); without framing you'd see nothing.)*
4. Navigate: **middle-drag** to pan, **scroll wheel** to zoom (0.25×–4×).

| Action | Control |
|---|---|
| Toggle Play↔Edit | **F1** |
| Pan / Zoom / Frame | **middle-drag** / **wheel** / **Home** |
| Select | **click** a sprite (outline appears) |
| Move/Rotate/Scale | **drag the gizmo handles** (tool + snap via toolbar) |
| Undo / Redo / Delete | **Z** / **Y** / **Delete** |
| Save / Load | toolbar buttons (writes/reads `editor_scene.json`) |

## One honest caveat about Save/Load

You can fully exercise **select · gizmo move/rotate/scale · snap · undo/redo · delete · camera nav** on the loaded level right now. But **Save/Load round-trip isn't hand-testable yet**: loaded level entities aren't tagged with `SceneObjectComponent` (only *editor-created* entities are), and there's no "create entity" UI yet — that's **Wave C (free placement)**. So the toolbar **Save** would currently write a near-empty scene. The round-trip *is* covered by the headless `SceneRoundTripGoldenTest` / `HeadlessEditorOpTest`, just not via the toolbar by hand.

If you want Save/Load to be hand-testable too, the smallest addition is a **"tag selected for saving"** toolbar action (mark a loaded entity as a save-root), or a minimal **"place a prop"** create action — either makes the persistence loop clickable without waiting for Wave C.

So — where to next?

Let's first nail what has been built so far. This is a screenshot after clicking to Edit Level 2 and pressing F1 and enabling the Colliders drawing checkbox in IMGUI: [Image #1]

1. It's cool that you added a button to edit the level right next to it, but actually the editor systems pipeline should be active in all game pipelines and be easily activated by a Run configuration flag I can set in Rider, and when this is active, I shouldn't need to press F1, it should be in Edit mode by default.
2. The game screen can be scaleddown and rendered in the center of the window, but the editor tools shouldn't overlay the game screen, but rather be placed around it, just like in Blender you have the viewport screen in the center and the menus to the side.
3. The tools are barely visible, I don't know if this is because of the white bg, but also we want the editor to be highres and readable, independent from the game resolution or fonts.
3. The idea of exploring ECS is that we don't have to care about specific implementations, whenever something has a Transform component, we should be able to attach a Gizmo to it to allow placement. But we should somehow be able to still have some behavior turned on while editing in realtime, like if another object is a parent/child of the object being moved, then it should move togheter. When I click to show the collider shapes, I can't drag the colliders, either this is a bug with Gizmo not showing or the collider doesn't have a Transform component and maybe just a DrawComponent/DrawElement? This should be solved, as I see it, everything with a position should have a Transform component. The DrawComponent/Element has it's own screen position, we need to think if that's still a good idea or not (we should think deeply about this and the implications to the usability and flexibility of the engine).
4. In the editor, we should be able to see the ECS systems pipeline and manually activate or deactivate them. Since the editor is now a gamedev concern, each system should somehow declare if it's enabled by default in edit mode: like we want follow system active, but collision system maybe not.

# MonoDreams Project Memory

## Project Structure (Post-Refactor)
- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library with rendering, camera, cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading
- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific: screens, input, dialogue, layout, settings, entity factories
- `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/` — isolated YarnSpinner integration (not referenced by core)
- Build: `dotnet build` for everything; individual projects can be built separately

## Key Architecture Decisions
- **EntityInfo** is string-based in core (`new EntityInfo("Player")`), Examples has `EntityType` enum convenience
- **Namespace conflicts**: `MonoDreams.EntityFactory` (not `.Entity`) to avoid shadowing `DefaultEcs.Entity`
- **CameraFollowTarget** lives in `MonoDreams.Component` (not Camera subdir) to avoid conflict with `Camera` class
- Core has no implicit usings — always add `using System;`, `using System.Collections.Generic;`, `using System.Linq;` when moving files from Examples to core

## Refactoring Patterns
- When moving files: use `cp` + `sed` (not cat/heredoc) so user can cache permissions in Claude Code
- Always `sed -i ''` on macOS (BSD sed requires empty string for in-place editing)
- After moving files from Examples to core, check for empty directories and remove them
- Build after every phase to catch issues early
- The plan was organized into phases with commits per phase for bisectability

## WAVE 6 SCOPE

**1. Editor pipeline registrar (level-editor module, reusable by any screen):**
- A registrar/builder where a screen registers each pipeline entry: `Add(name, ISystem<GameState> system, EditTimeBehavior policy, bool enabledInEditByDefault = policy!=Freeze)` (shape it sensibly). It:
  - builds the final `SequentialSystem<GameState>` wrapping entries in `GatedSystem` per policy,
  - **retains a runtime registry** (ordered list of entries: name, policy, gate/system refs, current enabled state) exposing `SetEnabled(name, bool)` / enumerate — the seam the Wave-8 systems panel will bind to. Wave 2 added the **native scene format** + the **component-serializer registry** (under `Serialization/`) and an additive `AssetKey` on `SpriteInfoComponent`. Wave 3 added the **scene round-trip** (`SceneObjectComponent`, `SceneWriter`, `LoadSceneRequest` + `SceneReaderSystem`, `IPlatformServices.ExportScene`). Wave 4a added the **interactive-editor substrate**: the reference `LevelEditorScreen` (in `MonoDreams.Examples.Core`) that composes the gated game pipeline + editor systems in one world with an in-place `RunMode` toggle; `SelectedComponent` + `EditorIdComponent` + `SelectionSystem` (click-to-pick the frontmost sprite); the `EditorHistory` bounded undo/redo with drag-coalescing + the `IEditorCommand` abstraction and the create/delete/transform commands; and the `EditorModeToggleSystem` / `EditorCommandSystem`. Wave 4b added the **transform gizmo** (`GizmoSystem` + `GizmoStateComponent` / `GizmoOverlayComponent` + the pure `Transform/GizmoTransform` math — move/rotate/scale handles, a selection outline, grid-snap, a drag coalesced into one undo step) and the **engine-native toolbar** (`ToolbarSystem` + `Component/ToolbarButtonComponent` + `UI/EditorToolbarBuilder` — tool-select/Save/Load/Undo/Redo/snap on the HUD target). Wave 5 added the **headless editor-op channel** (`Channel/EditorOpPlan` + `Channel/EditorOpReplaySystem`) plus the `CursorInputSystem.SkipHardwareRead` seam, so the real editor systems run headless with no real mouse. **Post-Wave-A usability** added **editor camera navigation** (`CameraNavSystem` + the pure `Navigation/CameraNav` math — middle-mouse pan, scroll-wheel zoom, and a frame-scene key that centres + zoom-fits the camera on all content so off-origin levels are reachable) and a **menu entry into the editor** (a per-level "Edit" button in `LevelSelectionScreen` that reuses the existing `ScreenTransitionRequest` → `RequestedLevelComponent` path to boot `LevelEditorScreen` on that level). **Wave 6** extracted the whole editor block into the reusable **composition seam** (under `Composition/`): the `EditorPipelineRegistrar` (named, gate-wrapped, runtime-toggleable pipeline entries — the systems panel's binding surface), the `EditorOverlay` (registry/serializer/history + every editor system + the toolbar + the headless channel, built over the screen's own world), and the `EditorRunFlag` (`--editor` / `MONODREAMS_EDITOR=1` — the plain game screen composes the overlay and the game boots in Edit). **Wave 7** added the **Blender-style editor shell**: in Edit the game composite renders into a smaller centered viewport (`ViewportManager.SetViewportInset` — compositing and mouse mapping follow the same rect) with the chrome placed *around* it at **native window resolution** (`RenderTargetID.Editor` + `EditorChromeRenderSystem` + `RenderLayer.Native`): opaque dark panels (top toolbar bar, right panel strip reserved for the Wave-8 systems panel, bottom strip — `UI/EditorChromeLayout` + `UI/EditorChromeBuilder`) and the toolbar rebuilt in real pixels (hit-testing raw `ScreenPosition`), all synced with the run mode by `EditorShellSystem` (which also swaps to the OS cursor over chrome in Edit). The old HUD-virtual toolbar builder is retired. **Wave 8a** made the overlay **universal** (under the run flag every Examples screen composes it — the menu and the infinite runner included; the overlay can supply its own cursor pipeline to a cursor-less screen via `provideCursorPipeline`), made selection + the gizmo **target-aware** (UI/HUD-target sprites hit-test/drag in virtual space via `VirtualPosition`; across targets the composite order wins — UI/HUD above Main; the gizmo overlays draw on the selected entity's own target), and shipped the **systems panel** (`System/SystemsPanelSystem` + the pure `UI/SystemsPanelLayout`) in the shell's right strip: every registrar entry of both pipelines, in order, as name + policy tag + live enabled checkbox, toggled through `EditorPipelineRegistrar.SetEnabled`. **Wave 8b** added the **collider gizmo proxies**: colliders are component-local spatial data (not entities), so `System/ProxySyncSystem` materializes standalone proxy entities (`GizmoProxyComponent` bindings under `Component/`, geometry under `Proxy/ProxyGeometry`) over the selected entity's collider shapes; they join the same selection pick (border-only hit-test) and the same gizmo drag (move tool), writing back into the bound component through `Undo/ColliderEditCommand` (one undo step per drag; convex writes refresh `WorldVertices`/`BroadPhaseAABB`). **Post-Wave-8b host wiring** extended the universal overlay **across hosts**: the Demos host (the launcher menu + all four module demo screens) composes it under the same run flag, pairing the overlay with the engine's new `DefaultEditorKeys` default keyboard surface (for hosts without their own action mapping) — the step-by-step recipe any new host/screen follows is [Adding the editor to a screen/host](#adding-the-editor-to-a-screenhost) below. Anything not yet built is marked **(planned, Wave N)**.

## ✅ Demos host wired — the editor is now genuinely host-agnostic

**On PR #31 (pushed):** `f47c093` → `c33c6e9`. **Verify:** core, Demos, and Examples.Desktop build 0 errors · **181 tests / 0 failed** (+6; the headless-demo contract tests pass unchanged, now env-leak-proofed by pinning `MONODREAMS_EDITOR=0` in the test runner unless a test opts in).

**What changed:**
- `MonoDreams.Demos` parses the same `--editor` / `MONODREAMS_EDITOR=1` flag; all 5 screens (launcher + camera/physics/dialogue/ui demos) build through the registrar and compose the overlay, booting in Edit. Demo simulations and — importantly — the demos' *own camera writers* freeze in Edit so they don't fight the editor's pan/zoom.
- A new engine-side **`DefaultEditorKeys`** surface (F1/Delete/Z/Y/Home) for hosts that lack their own action-mapping layer — that was the structural reason Demos couldn't just "get" the editor.
- The durable fix: the **"Adding the editor to a screen/host" recipe** now lives in the module docs (flag → registrar → overlay → boot RunMode), referenced from the flow doc and CORE_TENETS §9 — so the next host, or a future agent building one, follows four steps instead of rediscovering this.

One deviation worth knowing: `--headless --editor` **compose** (rather than the flag being ignored headless) — headless Demos renders every frame by design, which is also how the wiring was screenshot-verified: the camera demo's PNG shows the full shell, panel with `[freeze]` tags, inset viewport with the demo + minimap intact. The flag-off headless contract is untouched.

## READ FIRST (per .claude/CLAUDE.md)
- docs/CORE_TENETS.md (§9 editor tenet; ECS purity), docs/flows/level-editor.md, docs/flows/foundation.md.
- The ledger /Users/rodrigooliveira/.claude/implement/feat-level-editor/ledger.md — Directives + Wave 6/8a handoffs (registrar semantics: SetEnabled = both-modes master toggle on the gate's IsEnabled; the panel refuses to disable its own entry; entry naming `editor.*`).

- The panel: MonoDreams/level-editor/System/SystemsPanelSystem.cs + UI/SystemsPanelLayout.cs (pure layout — rows, scroll, hit-test) + how EditorChromeBuilder hosts it.
- ALL composition sites you must migrate (every screen that registers composite blocks): MonoDreams.Examples.Core/Screens/{LoadLevelExampleGameScreen,LevelSelectionScreen,InfiniteRunnerScreen}.cs (LevelEditorScreen is a thin subclass), MonoDreams.Demos screens ({DemoLauncherScreen,DemoScreens}.cs + DemoEditor.cs), and any composite the overlay itself registers.
- Tests to extend: MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/{EditorPipelineRegistrarTests,SystemsPanelTests}.cs (+ the composition-log integration tests in IntegrationTests/{UniversalOverlayTests,DemosEditorOverlayTests}.cs — keep their contract or update deliberately).

## SCOPE

**1. Hierarchical registrar (the structural fix):**
- Add group registration to `EditorPipelineRegistrar` — a group has a name, an edit-time policy (the gate wraps the WHOLE group, as today), a composite kind (Sequential or Parallel — input uses ParallelSystem in one path), and NAMED CHILDREN registered individually (arbitrary nesting depth). The registrar builds the composite itself (SequentialSystem/ParallelSystem of the children's built systems) and wraps it in the group's gate — screens stop pre-building opaque composites for anything they want visible. Design the API ergonomically (e.g. `AddGroup(name, policy, kind, g => { g.Add(...); g.AddGroup(...); })` or a begin/end builder — your call, keep it clean and match the existing style).
- Enabled semantics (document precisely as a premise): each LEAF keeps its own toggle handle (its gate's IsEnabled — decide whether leaves inside a group get individual gates or use the child system's own IsEnabled; prefer per-leaf gates for uniformity with today's 'every entry gate-wrapped' decision unless you find a real cost). A GROUP's checkbox state is DERIVED from its descendants: all enabled → checked; none → unchecked; mixed → indeterminate. Toggling a group sets ALL descendant leaves (Gmail convention: click on checked or indeterminate → all off; click on unchecked → all on — pick the Gmail/Material behavior and document it). `SetEnabled(name, bool)` keeps working for both leaves and groups (group = cascade); enumeration yields the tree (with depth) AND a flattened view for compatibility.
- Keep the existing flat `Add(...)` API working (single systems unchanged). Keep group gate policy semantics (Freeze on the group) exactly as today so run-mode behavior is unchanged by the migration.
- Preserve the 'panel refuses to disable its own entry' guard — extend it to any ANCESTOR group of the panel's entry.

**2. Migrate every composition site:** convert the opaque composite entries across the 3 Examples screens + 5 Demos screens + the overlay's own weave into named groups with named children (sensible child names: `logic.movement`, `logic.dialogue`, `levelLoad.ldtkEntities`, `prep.ySort`, etc. — mirror the class names). EVERY system that exists in a pipeline should be visible in the tree; if something must stay opaque (a genuine reason), document it in the premise. Run-mode behavior with the flag off/on must be byte-identical after migration (the whole existing suite must pass; the composition-log tests may need their expected entry lists updated — that's a deliberate contract update, note it).

**3. Panel tree UI (tri-state):**
- `SystemsPanelLayout` renders the tree: indentation per depth, groups before/above their children in pipeline order, leaf rows as today. Tri-state checkbox visuals: checked = filled + check, unchecked = empty, indeterminate = filled with a MINUS bar (the Gmail/Material pattern the user named). Group rows clickable exactly like leaves; hover, scroll, and the strip clamp behave as today. If the tree gets tall, the existing wheel-scroll covers it (collapse/expand is OPTIONAL — add only if cheap; otherwise note as follow-up).
- Policy tags: leaves show their effective policy; a group shows its gate policy (children inherit visual context via indentation — don't repeat the tag per child unless it differs).

## TESTS (failing-first)
- Registrar: group with children builds the right composite (Sequential vs Parallel) behind one gate; nested groups; leaf toggle stops exactly that system; group toggle cascades to all descendants; derived tri-state (all/none/mixed); Gmail click semantics; SetEnabled by name works for leaf + group; unknown name throws; panel-ancestor guard.
- Migration regression: run-mode gating unchanged (Freeze groups still freeze whole blocks in Edit); full suite green; composition-log tests updated deliberately if entry names changed.
- Panel: tree rows render with correct depth/order; tri-state states map to the right visual; clicking a group row cascades; clicking a leaf toggles one.
- Update the systems-panel + registrar premises (tri-state semantics, `Tests:` named).

  Claude-Session: https://claude.REDACTED
Push to origin feat/level-editor.
